messages:
Maya Patel: following up from today's all-hands Q&A 1 — collecting the process items so we can publish a short playbook and update PR templates. please keep replies tiny so i can paste them into the doc.

Gabe Nguyen: quick ones from my team: 1) are we introducing release freeze windows around major infra deploys? 2) what exact perf gates should block a rollout (we had one ambiguous merge yesterday).

Hannah Li: leadership guidance: no org-wide permanent freeze; instead we'll declare scoped freeze windows for major infra migrations (announced 2 weeks prior) and use a blocking tag for urgent fixes. routine releases keep the cadence (product = biweekly by default; infra may run weekly for low-risk fixes).

Hannah Li: perf gates: PRs touching serving/runtime must include bench artifacts (baseline + candidate). block if latency_p95 degrades >=12% OR memory_per_request increases >=12% OR qps drops >8% on comparable load. mention the load profile used.

Tomas Ortega: oncall clarification: primary rotation stays one week; secondary is a two-week shadow. handoffs should include a short summary line and any active mitigations. we're trialing a single pinned handoff post in #eng-oncall each Monday 09:00 PT.

Gabe Nguyen: SLAs for Dedicated customers came up — do we publish concrete latency numbers publicly and what happens when we automatically fall back?

Maya Patel: Dedicated customers have contract SLAs for uptime (99.9%) and agreed p95 latency targets. public guidance will show example buckets (small-seq p95 ~200ms; mid-context p95 ~350ms; long-context up to 600ms depending on model). automated fallback chains are enabled by default for critical routes (variant -> region -> degraded variant); customers will see a brief capacity-based degrade and we surface that in the incident timeline.

SRE-Shift: note: fallback chains will attempt model-family downgrade before cross-region failover. fallback is automatic for routes with fallback policy enabled; ops/SEs can opt-out per-customer in the contract.

Gabe Nguyen: can we get a short PR template snippet that enforces bench links and rollout plans? we want automation to fail the merge when artifacts are missing.

Hannah Li: draft snippet below (please suggest edits):
```
PR checklist (add to template):
- unit tests and basic integration smoke
- bench artifact links for baseline + candidate (must include exact load profile)
- perf diffs: latency_p95, latency_p99, qps, memory_per_request (block if p95 >= +12% OR memory >= +12% OR qps <= -8%)
- canary & rollback steps documented (who, how long, success criteria)
- security/data review if touching auth or customer data paths
```

ReleaseBot: canary lane created by @Hannah Li for release/1934 (canary window 18h).

Tomas Ortega: i'll publish the canonical metric ids and a tiny run script in #eng-sre by EOD tomorrow so teams can hook the checks into CI.

Maya Patel: thanks all. i'll run a 30-min follow-up office hours tomorrow 10:30am PT to walk through exception cases (hotfixes during freeze windows, how to document load profiles, and SLA FAQ text). i'll post the resulting playbook and action items in this thread. :thumbsup:
